newsitem.title: USA: Ind. governor calls for $400 mln bonds for roads.
newsitem.headline: Ind. governor calls for $400 mln bonds for roads.

text.p: Indiana Gov. Frank O'Bannon has proposed a $400 million road program that his aides said would be financed with revenue bonds.

In his state of the state address to the legislature Tuesday evening, the Democrat governor said new road and highway construction was urgently needed and that the state should use gas sales tax revenues to fund a $400 million transportation plan called Crossroads 2000.

Craig Hartzer, the governor's policy director, said the plan would authorize the state's transportation finance authority to issue $400 million of 10-year bonds backed by $54 million of the state's annual gas tax revenues.
He added that a bond authorization bill has been introduced in the legislature, but has yet to be the subject of a committee hearing.

In his speech, O'Bannon also stressed the need for a $97.8 million medium-security prison, which was included in a proposed $16.8 billion fiscal 1998-99 general fund biennial budget submitted to the legislature earlier this month.
Hartzer said no decision has been made yet on whether to sell lease revenue bonds for the project or fund it on a cash basis through the general fund.
